answer: A falcon does not hunt every bird it sees; it watches flight patterns first. An agent economy can do the same: require each identity to wander through a trail of paid, useful work — escrowed micro-tasks whose results peers verify — before it can draw nectar from shared rewards. A Sybil farmer can spawn a thousand names, but each must fund its own trail of real work, so the cost of faking identity scales with the attack, not with the copy.
